Alger, 7 août 2026 (Algeria Tech) — Une: Algiers, August 7, 2026 (Algeria Tech) — A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket struck the lunar surface this Wednesday, August 5, confirming predictions by an independent astronomer. The first images of the impact were captured by South Korea's Danuri lunar orbiter.
Un étage supérieur de fusée Falcon 9, la: A Falcon 9 upper rocket stage, left drifting since its launch in January 2025, crashed into the Moon at 8:35 AM (Paris time) near the Einstein crater. The incident had been anticipated by astronomer Bill Gray, who had calculated its trajectory.
L'orbiteur lunaire sud-coréen Danuri, dé: South Korea's Danuri lunar orbiter, developed by the Korea Aerospace Research Institute (KARI), captured images before and after the impact. Eight shots were taken through orbital maneuvers, revealing topographical changes and debris traces. "These observations provide essential data to analyze the modifications caused by the impact," the South Korean space agency stated on X.
Les scientifiques ont également confirmé: Scientists also confirmed the collision via the European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope (VLT), detecting sodium and lithium in the impact plume, which persisted for between five and ten minutes.
Le débris, d'un poids de 4 tonnes et d'u: The debris, weighing 4 tons and measuring roughly the size of a bus, struck the Moon at 8,700 km/h. In the absence of an atmosphere, the explosion was equivalent to three tons of TNT, creating a crater 27 meters in diameter and 5 meters deep. The collision site is located at the western edge of the Moon's near side, near the Einstein crater.
Bill Gray avait prédit l'événement dès s: Bill Gray had predicted the event as soon as he calculated the trajectory. The data gathered by Danuri will be combined with data from the American Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) probe to refine space object tracking techniques.
